title: Schönhage's Recursive HGCD: GCD Preservation and Matrix Invariants
description: Formalizes Schönhage's recursive half-GCD in Lean 4. Proves GCD preservation, det ±1 invariant, row-vector matrix invariant, entry bounds via Cramer's rule, and perturbation infrastructure toward O(M(n)·log n) complexity. One sorry for the size-reduction bound, which is blocked (false as stated for the current definition; requires a new `hgcdMatrixProper` with an identity base case for unbalanced inputs).

meta.author: Schönhage (1971), formalized in Lean 4
originalContributions: cofactor_mul_apply: cofactor multiplication composes the `apply` action — the algebraic composition law for Schönhage's recursive structure
hgcdMatrix_det_unit: every matrix returned by hgcdMatrix has det ±1, by induction on fuel using det_mul
hgcdMatrix_preserves_gcd: applying the HGCD matrix to (a, b) yields a pair with the same GCD — the operational correctness of Schönhage's HGCD
lehmerCofactors_invariant: row-vector invariant (a₀, b₀) · M = (current pair) is preserved across lehmerCofactors (Step 1 of size-reduction)
lehmerCofactors_invariant_le: strengthens the invariant with residue monotonicity max ahat' bhat' ≤ max ahat bhat (Step 2a)
row_vec_cramer: from (a₀, b₀) · M = (ahat, bhat) and det, derives a₀ · det = ahat · M.δ - bhat · M.γ (Cramer's rule for row convention)
entry_bound_of_even / entry_bound_of_odd: cofactor entries are bounded by the initial inputs under EvenPattern / OddPattern (Step 2b)
cofactor_apply_shift_decomp: decomposes M.apply(aHi·2^s + ea, bHi·2^s + eb) as 2^s · M.apply(aHi, bHi) + M.apply(ea, eb) (Step 3 key identity)
hgcdShift_pos / hgcdShift_top_lt: the half-bit shift is ≥ 1 for large inputs, and the top-half truncation strictly decreases max a b (induction foundations for Step 4)

overview.historicalContext: Arnold Schönhage (1971) extended Lehmer's cofactor-matrix technique by recursing on the top half of the bits. This half-GCD (HGCD) approach achieves O(M(n) log n) bit complexity when combined with fast multiplication M(n), making it the foundation of GMP's mpn_gcd for very large inputs. The key mathematical invariant is that the recursion maintains a unimodular (det = ±1) cofactor matrix that preserves the GCD, with the matrix entries bounded by the input size at each level of recursion.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize Schönhage's recursive half-GCD in Lean 4: define `hgcdMatrix : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → CofactorMatrix` (fuel-indexed for totality) and prove (A) GCD preservation and det ±1 unconditionally, and (B) size reduction — that applying the HGCD matrix halves the bit size of the input pair.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization is in two layers. Part A (correctness, 0 sorries): define `hgcdMatrix` fuel-indexed with `lehmerCofactors` as the base case, prove `det ±1` by induction on fuel using `det_mul`, and derive GCD preservation from the existing `cofactor_apply_gcd`. Part B (size reduction, 1 sorry): build 9 lemmas in 5 steps following Stehlé-Zimmermann (2004) — row-convention matrix invariant, residue monotonicity, Cramer entry bounds, perturbation decomposition, and shift-measure decrease for induction. The final Step 4 sorry is blocked: the theorem is false for the current `hgcdMatrix` definition (counterexample a=60, b=7 gives column output 421 vs. claimed bound 64), because the base case runs the full Euclidean algorithm for unbalanced inputs.
keyInsights: Fuel-indexing decouples correctness from termination: the correctness theorems (det ±1, GCD preservation) hold for any fuel value, regardless of whether the algorithm terminates 'naturally'. This is what makes the correctness layer clean.

The composition law cofactor_mul_apply is the new algebraic content: that (M₂ · M₁).apply(a, b) = M₂.apply(M₁.apply(a, b)). Implicit in the algorithm design but never explicitly stated in the parent file.

Convention dichotomy: `CofactorMatrix.apply` uses the column convention M · v. The size-reduction infrastructure requires the ROW convention v · M (tracking the current Euclidean pair). These agree for symmetric matrices (e.g., Fibonacci inputs with all quotients = 1) but diverge for general inputs.

The joint-bound theorem is FALSE as stated for the current algorithm: the base case runs the full Euclidean algorithm, giving column output O(a·b/gcd²) for unbalanced inputs. A correct size-reduction theorem requires `hgcdMatrixProper` with an identity base case (standard HGCD of Stehlé-Zimmermann 2004).
The entry bound (entries ≤ max(a, b)) IS provable for the base case via entry_bound_of_even/odd, but the column output bound requires a different algorithm.

sections.title: Part I: Composition of Cofactor Matrices
sections.summary: cofactor_mul_apply: matrix multiplication composes the apply action. Pure ring algebra.
sections.mathContext: $(M_2 \cdot M_1)(a, b) = M_2(M_1(a, b))$: the composition law that makes the recursive HGCD structure correct.

sections.title: Part II: Recursive HGCD Matrix Definition
sections.summary: Defines hgcdMatrix (fuel-indexed, total), hgcdMatrixOf, and reduction equations for proofs. The recursion structure follows Schönhage: top-half subproblem M₁, apply to full precision, bottom-half subproblem M₂, compose M₂ · M₁.
sections.mathContext: Schönhage's HGCD computes a cofactor matrix by recursing on the top $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ bits: solve the subproblem on $\lfloor a/2^s \rfloor, \lfloor b/2^s \rfloor$, apply to full precision, recurse on the reduced pair. Fuel indexing ensures totality.

sections.title: Part III: Determinant Is ±1
sections.summary: hgcdMatrix_det_unit: every matrix from hgcdMatrix has det ±1. Induction on fuel: base is identity (det 1); recursive uses det_mul and IH twice.
sections.mathContext: The determinant invariant $\det(M) = \pm 1$ is the key algebraic property guaranteeing GCD preservation. It is maintained inductively: each level multiplies two ±1-determinant matrices via $\det(M_2 \cdot M_1) = \det M_2 \cdot \det M_1$.

sections.title: Part IV: GCD Preservation
sections.summary: hgcdMatrix_preserves_gcd: applying the HGCD matrix to (a, b) yields a pair with the same Int.gcd. Direct corollary of cofactor_apply_gcd and the det ±1 invariant.
sections.mathContext: Since $\det(M) = \pm 1$, the matrix is invertible over $\mathbb{Z}$, so $\gcd(M(a,b)) = \gcd(a,b)$. This is the operational correctness statement of Schönhage's HGCD — any GCD computation on the post-HGCD pair gives the same answer as on the original.

sections.title: Part V.5: Matrix-Vector Invariant and Residue Monotonicity
sections.summary: Row-convention invariant: (a₀, b₀) · M = (current pair) persists across lehmerCofactors. Residue monotonicity: max ahat' bhat' ≤ max ahat bhat at each step. Steps 1 and 2a of the size-reduction proof.
sections.mathContext: The Lehmer algorithm accumulates M via right-multiplication: $M' = M \cdot S_q$ where $S_q = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&-q\end{pmatrix}$. This preserves the ROW invariant $(a_0, b_0) \cdot M = (\hat{a}_k, \hat{b}_k)$ (current residues). Each step also satisfies $\hat{b}' < \hat{b}$, so the max is non-increasing.

sections.title: Part VI: Cramer Identity and Entry Bounds
sections.summary: row_vec_cramer: Cramer's rule in the row convention. EvenPattern / OddPattern alternation. entry_bound_of_even / entry_bound_of_odd: matrix entries are bounded by the initial inputs. Step 2b.
sections.mathContext: From $(a_0, b_0) \cdot M = (\hat{a}, \hat{b})$ and $\det M = \pm 1$, Cramer's rule gives $a_0 \cdot \det M = \hat{a} \cdot M.\delta - \hat{b} \cdot M.\gamma$. The sign pattern (EvenPattern / OddPattern) alternates with each Euclidean step. Combined, this gives $|M.\alpha|, |M.\beta| \leq b_0$ and $|M.\gamma|, |M.\delta| \leq a_0$.

sections.title: Part VII: Perturbation Infrastructure
sections.summary: cofactor_apply_shift_decomp: M.apply(aHi·2^s + ea, bHi·2^s + eb) = 2^s · M.apply(aHi,bHi) + M.apply(ea,eb). Error bounds via triangle inequality. Step 3 building blocks.
sections.mathContext: Writing $a = a_{\text{Hi}} \cdot 2^s + e_a$ with $0 \leq e_a < 2^s$, linearity of `apply` gives a clean signal+error decomposition. The error term $M(e_a, e_b)$ is bounded by $2 \cdot \text{max\_entry} \cdot 2^s$ using the Step 2b entry bounds.

sections.title: Part VIII: Shift Bounds for Induction
sections.summary: hgcdShift_pos: shift ≥ 1 for inputs ≥ 4. hgcdShift_top_lt: top-half truncation strictly decreases max a b. These enable strong induction on max a b for Step 4.
sections.mathContext: $s = \lceil (\log_2 \max(a,b)) / 2 \rceil \geq 1$ for $\max(a,b) \geq 4$, so $2^s \geq 2$, and $\max(a/2^s, b/2^s) < \max(a,b)$ by integer division.

sections.title: Part IX: Size-Reduction Claim (Blocked)
sections.summary: The joint bound (column output and entries ≤ 2^(s+3)) is FALSE for the current hgcdMatrix. native_decide counterexample: a=60, b=7 gives column output 421 vs. claimed bound 64. Blocked pending a new hgcdMatrixProper definition.
sections.mathContext: The current `hgcdMatrix` runs the full Euclidean algorithm in the base case, giving column output $O(a \cdot b / \gcd^2)$ for unbalanced inputs. A correct size-reduction theorem requires `hgcdMatrixProper` (Stehlé-Zimmermann 2004) with an identity base case when $b < 2^{s}$, ensuring the algorithm only runs approximately half the Euclidean steps.

conclusion.summary: The correctness layer of Schönhage's recursive HGCD is fully formalized: `hgcdMatrix` always has det ±1 and preserves GCD. The size-reduction infrastructure (Steps 1–3) is built, but the joint bound (Step 4) is blocked because the theorem is false for the current algorithm definition.

openQuestions.question: Can `hgcdMatrix` be redefined with an identity base case for imbalanced inputs (b < 2^(hgcdShift a b)) to make `hgcdMatrix_joint_bound` provable?
openQuestions.significance: This would complete Step 4 of the size-reduction proof and establish the halving property of HGCD.

openQuestions.question: Can the full O(M(n)·log n) bit complexity be formalized once a Mathlib bit-complexity model and fast multiplication are available?
openQuestions.significance: Would fully answer the original open question of Schönhage's complexity claim.
